If you have ten minutes tomorrow, I will send you the itinerary.
If I were in your position, I would start with a pilot.
If we had more time, I would take you to the coast.
If you could change one thing about your system, what would it be?
You must be exhausted. How was the flight — did you come through Dubai, or the other way round?
Through Dubai. Twenty-six hours. The jet lag will hit me tomorrow, not tonight.
Then we will keep tomorrow morning light. Have you been to Brazil before, or is this the first time?
First time. I have been to Lisbon twice, which people tell me is not the same thing at all.

It is not, but you already have the language. I lived in Lisbon for a year, so we have common ground already. If I were you I would order the fish tonight — it is the one thing this cuisine does better than anywhere.
Then I will have the fish. And what would you do with a free Sunday here, if you had one?
If we had more time I would take you up the coast, but you have a Friday flight. So my recommendation would be the market in the morning and nothing at all in the afternoon.
Nothing at all sounds ambitious. Tell me about the year in Lisbon — what took you there?
How was the flight? Did you come through Dubai, or the other way round?
If I were you, I would order the fish tonight.
If you had a free day here, what would you want to see?
If it were up to me we would go into that now, but I would rather show you properly on Tuesday.
It has been a long day for you. Shall we pick this up tomorrow?

The thing nobody tells you about a business dinner is that the first twenty minutes decide the whole evening, and almost nobody prepares for them. People prepare the pitch. Nobody prepares the small talk. I have sat at tables where somebody brought up the contract before the starters arrived, and you could feel the temperature drop. What I do now, and I would recommend this to anyone, is I find one thing before I get there. One thing. Where they went to university, a city we have both lived in, a team they support. If I were starting again, that is the only skill I would work on, because everything else you can prepare on a plane. And read the room. If the table goes quiet after somebody mentions work, that is information. Do not fill the silence with more work.

I would not say one is better than the other, but they are not the same evening. With some of the partners I work with, dinner is the meeting. Nothing is signed at the table, nothing is even discussed at the table, and then two days later everything moves, and it moves because of the dinner. With others, dinner is genuinely dinner. It is forty minutes, it is friendly, and then somebody says right, shall we talk about the numbers. The mistake I made for years was assuming, and if I could give myself one piece of advice it would be this: ask. Ask the person who invited you what the evening is for. Nobody has ever been offended by that question, and I have been wrong about it more often than I have been right.
